name: Amanemu
insider_take: This secluded ryokan-inspired sanctuary sits within Ago-Shima National Park, where ancient traditions meet pristine natural beauty on Japan's sacred Shima Peninsula.
whats_special: Amanemu is built around natural hot springs sourced from 1,000 meters underground, offering therapeutic mineral-rich waters in private onsen pavilions. The resort overlooks Ago Bay, famous for its cultured pearl farms and traditional ama (female divers) who still harvest seafood using centuries-old techniques. Each suite features traditional Japanese architecture with modern luxury, including private gardens and some with dedicated onsen.
pro_tip: Book the Pearl Season experience (December-February) when you can witness the legendary ama divers in action and participate in pearl harvesting alongside these remarkable women who hold their breath for up to two minutes.
dont_miss: The sunrise meditation at the resort's clifftop pavilion, where you can watch the mist rise over Ago Bay's 60 small islands. Visit nearby Ise Grand Shrine, Japan's most sacred Shinto site, just 30 minutes away. The resort's signature kaiseki dining features ultra-fresh seafood from local ama divers and Matsusaka beef from the region.
pros: Traditional Japanese ryokan-style luxury with private onsen hot springs
Stunning location overlooking Ago Bay in Ise-Shima National Park
Exceptional personalized service and attention to detail
World-class spa treatments incorporating local wellness traditions
cons: Ultra-luxury pricing reflecting exclusive Aman brand positioning
Remote location requires additional travel time from major cities
